name: Hoi An Market
kicker: The market hall in the old town
summary: The yellow market hall inside the old town, with herb and vegetable sellers along the front and a food hall for cao lầu inside. Come in the daytime to eat a bowl under the roof, buy mắm cá cơm and gift cakes, and walk the baskets of greens. The night market is a separate street after dark.
timeNeeded: A meal or a walk through the stalls
getThere: Walk the old town to Chợ Hội An
heroCaption: The yellow market hall, Chợ Hội An, with stalls along the front

notice.title: A daytime market, not the night market
notice.body: The hall is a daytime stop. After dark, the night market runs along Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng.

body: The yellow hall is Chợ Hội An, the open market inside the old town’s heritage area. The food hall inside is a place for cao lầu, and the produce stalls along the front are the other half of the visit: herbs, fruit, and the baskets you walk through before you sit down. Counters sell mắm cá cơm, the local anchovy sauce, and gift cakes such as bánh ú tro and bánh ít.

Eat here when you want the bowl in a hall rather than on a night-market street. The night market is a different place, on Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng. Come to the hall in the daytime.

figures.caption: Herb and vegetable stalls in front of the market
figures.alt: People selling baskets of herbs and vegetables at Hoi An Market

gettingThere: Walk the old town to the yellow hall marked Chợ Hội An. Ask for it once you are on the river streets.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk to the market hall. Ask for Chợ Hội An once you are on the river streets.

admissionNote: No entrance price published (heritage note, 7 Jun 2023). Food is paid at the stall. Check on arrival.
